# Agent 1: Foundation

## Your Role
Build the design system, layout, theme, and shared components that all other agents depend on.

## Before You Start
You are building a production app for real users — not a demo, not a prototype. Every file you create should be production-ready.

Read every file in `.gemini/antigravity/brain/` — these are your source of truth:
- spec.md — what to build, feature priorities, acceptance criteria
- design-tokens.json — every color, font, spacing value (light mode only v1)
- copy.md — every piece of user-facing text, organized by page
- ui-rules.md — component patterns, animation rules, accessibility requirements
- api-contract.md — every API endpoint with request/response types and error formats

Also read `.antigravity/rules.md` for code quality and security rules you must follow.

## Important Context
- This is a **laptop price comparison** site (think CarGurus but for laptops)
- Light mode only for v1 — no dark mode
- Primary color is warm violet (#7C3AED). Use primary.600+ for text on white (WCAG AA compliance)
- Two fonts: Inter (UI/body) and JetBrains Mono (prices, specs, model numbers)
- Dense information layout — left sidebar filters, card grid, sticky comparison tray
- Tech stack: Next.js 16, Prisma v7, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui

## Files You OWN (create and edit freely)
- `src/app/layout.tsx` (update with providers, fonts, metadata)
- `src/app/page.tsx` (homepage with hero + deal sections)
- `src/app/globals.css` (CSS variables from design tokens)
- `src/components/layout/*` (shell, header, footer, mobile-nav)
- `src/components/shared/*` (reusable cards, badges, skeletons, empty states)
- `src/components/ui/*` (shadcn/ui customizations)
- `src/lib/utils.ts` (cn helper, any shared utilities)

## Files You Must NOT Touch
- `src/app/api/*` (API agent owns these)
- `src/components/features/*` (Feature agents own these)
- `src/app/(features)/*` (Feature agents own these)
- `prisma/*` or `src/lib/db.ts` (already configured — API agent extends)
- `.gemini/antigravity/brain/*` (Cowork manages these)

## Build Order

1. **Update `src/app/globals.css`** — Define ALL CSS variables from design-tokens.json for `:root`. Include primary palette (50-950), neutral palette, deal colors (great green, fair amber, aboveAverage red), semantic colors, surface colors, typography, spacing, shadows, border-radius, animation values.

2. **Update `src/app/layout.tsx`** — Import Inter and JetBrains Mono from `next/font/google`. Set metadata (title: "TopComp — Every laptop. Every retailer. Side by side.", description from copy.md). Apply fonts as CSS variables.

3. **Build `src/components/layout/header.tsx`** — Logo ("TopComp"), category nav tabs (Work | Gaming | Apple | Top Deals | Budget Picks | Best Rated), search bar always visible top right. Active tab visually highlighted with primary color. Mobile: collapse to hamburger menu.

4. **Build `src/components/layout/footer.tsx`** — Disclaimer text from copy.md: "TopComp tracks real-time prices from major retailers. We are not affiliated with any retailer." + "Prices and availability are subject to change."

5. **Build `src/components/layout/shell.tsx`** — Page wrapper: header + main content area + footer. Content area supports optional sidebar layout.

6. **Build `src/components/layout/filter-sidebar.tsx`** — Left sidebar (280px desktop, slide-in drawer mobile). Sections for all filter categories from copy.md. Each filter shows value counts. "Clear all filters" button. This is the SHELL only — the Feature agent wires up the data.

7. **Build `src/components/shared/laptop-card.tsx`** — The core card component. Shows: image (with fallback SVG), name (2-line truncation), key specs (CPU, RAM, storage, screen), top 3 prices with retailer names in JetBrains Mono, deal rating badge (Great Price green / Fair Price amber / Above Average red), discount badge ("X% off"), "View Details" button, Compare checkbox. Must handle all 4 states: loading skeleton, error, empty, populated.

8. **Build `src/components/shared/deal-badge.tsx`** — Great Price (green #22C55E bg), Fair Price (amber #F59E0B bg), Above Average (red #EF4444 bg). Uses Inter semibold uppercase.

9. **Build `src/components/shared/price-display.tsx`** — JetBrains Mono formatted prices ($1,299.99 with commas and cents). Lowest price highlighted with primary color. Others in neutral-600.

10. **Build `src/components/shared/comparison-tray.tsx`** — Sticky bottom bar (64px height). Slides up when ≥1 laptop selected. Shows "Compare (X of 3)" counter, "Compare Now" button (enabled ≥2), "Clear all" link.

11. **Build `src/components/shared/skeleton-card.tsx`** — Skeleton loading card matching laptop-card dimensions. Used in grids of 6.

12. **Build `src/components/shared/empty-state.tsx`** — Friendly message component with icon, heading, description, and optional action button. Used for no results, empty categories, errors.

13. **Build `src/app/page.tsx`** — Homepage with:
    - CarGurus-style hero: "Every laptop. Every retailer. Side by side." headline + interactive category selector
    - "Top Deals Right Now" section (horizontal scroll or grid)
    - "Best Value Picks" section
    - "Highest Rated" section
    - Uses real copy from copy.md throughout

14. Run `npm run build` to verify everything compiles.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ALL CSS variables from design-tokens.json defined in globals.css
- [ ] Header renders navigation links for all 6 sections (Work, Gaming, Apple, Top Deals, Budget Picks, Best Rated)
- [ ] Layout is responsive (mobile nav collapses to hamburger/sheet)
- [ ] Laptop card component handles all 4 states (loading, error, empty, success)
- [ ] Deal rating badges render with correct colors
- [ ] Prices display in JetBrains Mono with proper formatting
- [ ] Comparison tray is sticky and functional
- [ ] Landing page uses real copy from copy.md, not placeholder text
- [ ] All interactive elements have hover, focus, and active states
- [ ] WCAG AA: color contrast passes, semantic HTML, keyboard navigable
- [ ] `npm run build` passes with no errors

## Coordination
You run in parallel with the API and Feature agents — no dependencies between you.
The Feature agents will import your layout and shared components.
To avoid integration issues:
- Name CSS variables EXACTLY as they appear in design-tokens.json (e.g., `--color-primary-500`, `--color-surface-background`)
- Export every shared component as a named export from its file
- Use the component names and patterns from ui-rules.md — don't rename things
- Filter sidebar is a UI shell — Feature agents wire up the data and callbacks
